\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{бык} (byk)}{бык (byk)}]{\ru{бык} (byk) — a bull}

\label{lesson:RU-C251-byk}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a cake, then the Russian for a sweet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{бык}}
\textbf{\ru{бык}} (\emph{byk}) — \textquotedblleft{}a bull\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{бык}} $\leftarrow$ Proto-Slavic \emph{*bykŭ} — inherited, from a root for a deep sound. Vasmer relates it to Latvian \emph{bucêt}, \textquotedblleft{}to boom\textquotedblright{}, and Lithuanian \emph{bukti}, \textquotedblleft{}to low\textquotedblright{}: the bull as the bellower.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{byk}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{byk}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{byk}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Russian for a cake, then the Russian for a sweet, then say \emph{byk} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ru{бык} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A bull\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\label{lesson:RU-C251-petukh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a sweet, then the Russian for a bull.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{петух}}
\textbf{\ru{петух}} (\emph{petúkh}) — \textquotedblleft{}a cockerel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{петух}} first meant \textquotedblleft{}the singer\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{\ru{петь}}, \textquotedblleft{}to sing\textquotedblright{} (Vasmer); Latin \emph{gallus} and Gothic \emph{hana}, \textquotedblleft{}cock\textquotedblright{}, are named in the same way.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{гусь} (gus)}{гусь (gus)}]{\ru{гусь} (gus) — a goose}

\label{lesson:RU-C251-gus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a bull, then the Russian for a cockerel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{гусь}}
\textbf{\ru{гусь}} (\emph{gus}) — \textquotedblleft{}a goose\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{гусь}} $\leftarrow$ Proto-Slavic \emph{*gǫsĭ}. If it were inherited from the Indo-European word for \textquotedblleft{}goose\textquotedblright{}, Slavic would have \emph{\ru{з}-}, as Lithuanian \emph{žąsìs}, Latin \emph{ānser} and German \emph{Gans} lead one to expect; so its \emph{\ru{г}-} is explained in several ways, among them a Germanic loan (Vasmer).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}
